title: Why AI music is getting labelled on streaming sites
description:
What would you do if you found out that your favourite artist was not actually human? More musicians are using AI-tools for their work. But recently, there has also been a boom in AI Personas and 100% AI generated work. Some fans and musicians are not happy, they have called for more transparency around what’s human made. Streaming websites have also raised concerns about fraud and copyright infringement. Tidal and Deezer have outright banned the promotion of this AI content. And now Spotify has announced it will begin labelling songs that are AI generated.

BBC Newsbeat journalist, Eleanor Doyle, talks us through how you can spot AI generated music, how it has made and how regulating it on streaming platforms might work.

Plus, we also hear from two musicians, Marina Josephina in the UK, and Nkasiobi Chukwu in Nigeria about their experiences with AI music.

summaryEn: This episode of What in the World explores the rise of AI-generated music on streaming platforms and the efforts to regulate it through clearer labeling. UK singer Marina Josefina shares her frustration after discovering an artist she enjoyed was entirely AI-generated, while Nigerian producer Nsikak discusses how AI lowers barriers to music creation while creating economic and copyright challenges for human artists. BBC journalist Eleanor Doyle explains how AI music is created and spotted, and details how platforms like Spotify, Deezer, and Apple Music are implementing AI badges, self-disclosure requirements, and recommendation restrictions to increase transparency for listeners.
